variants: R1 AIR, R1, and R1 EDU on the product page, which lists secondary development for the R1 EDU only. The shop sells the R1 AIR and R1 in white and red, and takes the R1 EDU by contacting sales.
availability_note: Unitree's product page lists the R1 AIR, R1 and R1 EDU, with the EDU marked contact sales. The shop page shows an add-to-cart control and says the R1 Air (White) is backordered and will ship as soon as it is back in stock.

hardware.compute: An 8-core high-performance processor. A high-power computing module is an accessory of the R1 EDU, with multiple brands and models available such as Orin (40-100 TOPS).
hardware.sensors: A four-microphone array and a speaker, with a monocular camera on the R1 AIR and a binocular camera on the R1 and R1 EDU. WiFi 6 and Bluetooth 5.2 are listed as present, and the page describes a two-degree-of-freedom head for environmental perception.
hardware.actuation: Low-inertia high-speed internal-rotor permanent magnet synchronous motors on crossed roller bearings and double-hook ball bearings. The page lists 20 degrees of freedom on the R1 AIR, 26 on the R1, and 26 to 40 on the R1 EDU, made up of six per leg, four or five per arm, two at the waist, and two at the head. It states an arm load of about 2 kg, a standing size of 1230 x 357 x 190 mm, a weight of about 27 kg with battery on the AIR and about 29 kg on the others, a calf-plus-thigh length of 600 mm and a forearm-plus-upper-arm length of 420 mm, knee motion from -10 to +139 degrees, hip yaw of plus or minus 157 degrees, pitch of -168 to +146 degrees and roll of -60 to +100 degrees, and waist yaw of plus or minus 150 degrees and roll of plus or minus 30 degrees. Electrical routing is hollow plus internal routing and the joint encoders are dual plus single.
hardware.power: A lithium battery with about one hour of battery life. A quick-release smart battery and a charger are accessories, and cooling is local air cooling.

developer_access: Unitree's product page states that the R1's joint and sensor control interfaces are fully open and that mainstream simulation platforms are supported, and lists secondary development for the R1 EDU. Its unitree_rl_mjlab repository names the R1 among the robots it supports, offers a Unitree-R1-Flat velocity-tracking task, and carries a deploy/robots/r1 program with a velocity policy configuration, documented through the same Train, Play, Sim2Real workflow. Its unitree_sdk2 repository ships an r1 example directory with low-level joint examples, a high-level locomotion client, and an audio client.
terms_note: Unitree's SDK, unitree_sdk2, is released under the BSD 3-Clause License. Unitree's terms page has Terms, After-sales Terms, Privacy Policy, Disclaimer, and End User License Agreement tabs; the after-sales tab is the hardware warranty policy, and the licence agreement is offered as a downloadable document rather than as page text. The product page lists a 6-month warranty for the R1 AIR, 8 months for the R1, and 12 months for the R1 EDU.
not_verified: The documented policy interfaces are Unitree's own claims; the Atlas has not verified them. Every source is a Unitree web page or repository file that Unitree can change at any time.
